title: Elon Musk on AI abundance, robots, long-term control and incentive structures (The Economist)
summary: Long Economist interview where Musk lays out his view of a 2036 AI and robotics economy, what constrains AI (power and chips), and why he keeps voting control to invest on 5-10 year horizons. Large parts are political debate with little business insight.

principles.text: Think of the economy as digital intelligence plus physical intelligence; robots are the end effectors that turn AI into atoms.
principles.quote: you can really think of the economy as uh digital and physical intelligence.

principles.text: The real constraints on AI are electricity and chips, so find the binding constraint and build around it.
principles.quote: the constraints on AI are essentially electricity and AI chips.

principles.text: Protect your ability to invest on 5-10 year horizons; quarterly earnings pressure punishes long-payoff bets.
principles.quote: I really just need to make sure that I can focus on long-term by longterm I just mean in the 5 to 10 years.

principles.text: Understand the incentive structure and the behavior of others follows from it.
principles.quote: So once you in understand the incentive structure, the behavior naturally follows.

principles.text: Competitors can keep each other honest, because each has an incentive to catch the others' problems.
principles.quote: all the competitors have an incentive to keep the others honest.

principles.text: A company without a creative visionary risks making good products but no breakthrough ones.
principles.quote: when you don't have a creative genius like Steve Jobs, you don't you you what what you miss what what Apple's missing are the incredible breakthrough products.
